title: Your body rule
hook: one page for the body: Francis called his body Brother Ass, and at the end asked it to forgive him
tomorrow: the wedding night everyone feared: what did Tobias do first?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: care. Tie the camel, then trust. This week's lines come back in the games: move daily, eat with care, breathe, here I am, rest, care. Today they go on one page.

Some people talk to their body like a boss to a worker who's slacking: come on, push through. Francis of Assisi did something like that for years. He fasted hard, slept on the ground, wore rough cloth, and called his body Brother Ass, a donkey to be driven hard and fed little. Near the end of his life, sick and worn out, he said something very different to it.
screen: `COME ON, PUSH THROUGH.` → `FRANCIS FASTS AND SLEEPS ON THE GROUND.` → `BROTHER ASS.` → `NEAR THE END, SOMETHING DIFFERENT.`

segments.voice: His early biographer, Thomas of Celano, tells it. Francis admitted he had sinned against Brother Body, and asked it to forgive him. Rejoice, he told it, and forgive me. Notice the word that stayed: brother. Even the donkey was a brother. Francis could be fierce with his body, but at the end he spoke to it as a companion he'd driven too hard. That's a Christian teaching older than Francis. Paul writes to the church at Corinth: "know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you." In Paul's picture, the body isn't a shell the soul wears. It's a dwelling place. In Christian worship, the body kneels and stands, fasts and feasts: it's part of the prayer. Francis's late apology sits easily beside that old verse. So here's the week, gathered. Sleep first, like Jesus in the stern. Move daily, with the grain, like Cook Ding's knife. Eat with care, blessing when full. Breathe, with something for the breath to carry. Here I am, from the feet up. Rest, the bow unstrung. Care, the rope and the trust. One page for the body is a way of never needing to say sorry to it at the end.
screen: `FRANCIS: FORGIVE ME, BROTHER BODY.` · `THE BODY IS THE TEMPLE.` · `KNEEL, STAND, FAST, FEAST.` · `THE WEEK ON ONE PAGE.` · then, large: `THIS BODY.`

segments.voice: Take one page and write a short line for each: sleep, movement, food, breath, scan, rest, care. Keep each line small enough to keep. Then sit with the page on your lap, both hands resting on it, for the rest of the time.
Your body rule: one page for the body, sleep to care, written for a brother, not a donkey.
Your line: this body. Francis called it brother, and asked its pardon at the end. Day 1652, and the body's page is written.

howItsDone: Christians speak of the body as a temple of the Holy Spirit, and Franciscans remember Francis calling it Brother Body. A personal rule of life often has a short page for the body: sleep, movement, food, breath, rest and care.
